svg.text: Analysis of 11 November 2026 · 7-iron · 120 fps · range after work
Decided by the rule table, from Plates I and II

text.tspan: Your hips moved toward the ball by 7% of your body height between address and impact.

The last still moment before takeaway. Body lines drawn from the pose in
your swing clip.
Your hips have left the address line, moving toward the ball. Hips, knees
and ankles were clearly visible in both frames.
ory, this was a clean clip: 120 fps, your whole body
in frame, and every point we needed was visible at
address and at impact. At address your backside sits on
the line we drew straight up from it. By impact your hips have moved 7%
of your body height past that line, toward the ball². When the hips push
forward, your chest rises with them and the club has less room to come
from the inside, which often shows up as thin or blocked shots. The
likely reason is that your lead hip is not turning far enough: 31° at
impact, where about 45° is typical¹. Turn more, and the hips no longer
have to push forward to make room for your arms.
“It may feel like you stay down, but at
impact your hips have moved toward the ball.”

svg.text: Feel cue · compare Plate I with Plate II

text.tspan: Set up with your backside touching a wall, or
your golf bag. Make slow half swings, keeping
your trail glute on the wall through impact.

svg.text: Fixes: hips move toward the ball²

text.tspan: Sit with both knees bent to 90°, one leg in front
of you and one to the side. Rotate slowly from
one side to the other. Works on the likely cause:
restricted hip rotation¹.

svg.text: Generic guidance, not medical advice — see a physiotherapist if you feel pain.

text.tspan: Your posture angle changed 6° in the downswing. That is past the potential
threshold (5°) but well short of the fault threshold (9°), so there is no drill
for it. Worth watching on your next clip.
Your hand path in transition stayed on or below the backswing path. Over the
top is capped at medium confidence while it is measured from the hand path,
without club tracking.

Answers are based only on this analysis.

text.tspan: Why does it feel like I’m staying down
when I’m not?
Your hips move forward rather than up, and
forward is hard to feel. In Plate II your hips
sit 7% of your body height closer to the ball
than at address². The wall drill makes it
something you can feel: if your trail glute
leaves the wall before impact, that is the
movement the video shows.
Will this fix my slice?
I can’t tell from this analysis. It reads your
body in the video, not the ball flight. Over
the top was checked and not found (medium).
